name: חֹבָב
summary: Hobab, “the son of Reuel the Midianite”, of Moses' family by marriage, whom Moses asked to go with Israel from Sinai and be eyes for them in the wilderness, promising him a share of the good Yahweh would do to Israel (Num 10:29–32); his descendants the Kenites went up with Judah and lived among Israel (Jdg 1:16; 4:11). The name has the letters of חָבַב “love”, whose participle חֹבֵב differs from it only in the last vowel (Deu 33:3), and answers to Arabic ḥubāb and ḥabīb, “beloved”; whether it means “beloved” or “one who loves”, the form does not settle.

evidence.note: Moses said לְחֹבָב בֶּן־רְעוּאֵל הַמִּדְיָנִי חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה: “Go with us, and we will do you good.”
He would go back to his own land; Moses presses him: “you shall be to us for eyes.”
Heber the Kenite had separated from the sons of חֹבָב חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה.
The sons of the Kenite, Moses' חֹתֵן, went up with Judah from the city of palms.
The root's verb: אַף חֹבֵב עַמִּים, “yes, he loves the peoples”: the same consonants as the name.

note: Num 10:29 can be read with Hobab or Reuel as Moses' חֹתֵן; Jdg 4:11 gives the title to Hobab. Exo 2:18 names Zipporah's father Reuel, and Exo 3:1 calls Moses' חֹתֵן Jethro; TIPNR takes Hobab as Jethro's son. Whether חֹתֵן here means father-in-law or a wider in-law is left to the reviewer.
